notes: §1985:VI.6.12.4 GR2: "Implementors will specify, for their compilers, all details on how the other language(s) are to be written." WiseOwl specifies no other language, so there is nothing to write in one. WiseOwl does not provide ENTER: §1985:I.1.5.2.5.5 "may include the ENTER statement or not, at the option of the implementor", and docs/conformance/3.7.1 records the decision (no language-name specified, §1985:VI.6.12.3 SR1); kb/Work PB5373 class 3 decides this row DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT and PB5308 landed the refusal. StatementBinder#BindEnter (reached from BindStatementCore for every enterStatement) refuses each ENTER at 85 with COBOL7240, so no other-language text is compiled or run. Probed at --std 85 (work-rd-03): class b, ENTER FORTRAN SUBRTN., ENTER ASSEMBLER., ENTER C SUBRTN., ENTER LINKAGE SUBRTN., ENTER COBOL., ENTER FORTRAN. ... ENTER COBOL. (both lines COBOL7240), the statement twice (two COBOL7240), inside IF and in an unreachable paragraph (COBOL7240), exit 65 and nothing printed; ENTER. and ENTER "FORTRAN" are COBOL0001; in-line text after ENTER FORTRAN is COBOL0001. Class c: at 2002/2014/2023 COBOL0902 plus COBOL7240 (the double report is kb/Work PB5538, not a 1985 defect). Classes a, d, e, f do not apply (no data, file or arithmetic operand). Witness: the refusal 1985-SR-VI_6_12_3-1 (COBOL7240 at 85). These general rules state what a provided ENTER does, which is the non-supported element itself. The independent refuter (op-20261114/out-read6/rd-03-refute.json) judged the category: "DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT. The 1985 text offers the choice at the level of the whole statement: §1985:I.1.5.2.5.5 "An implementation of Standard COBOL may include the ENTER statement or not, at the option of the implementor." It does not offer an implementation that includes ENTER with an empty set of languages. WiseOwl takes the 'not' arm (docs/conformance/3.7.1; StatementBinder.BindEnter refuses every ENTER with COBOL7240 at --std 85, probed: refute-rd-03/e1.cob `ENTER COBOL.` and e2.cob `ENTER FORTRAN SUB1.` + `ENTER COBOL.`, each COBOL7240, exit 65). GR1 ("The other language statements are executed in the object program as if they had been compiled into the object program following the ENTER statement") and GR3 ("routine-name-1 is given to identify the portion of the other language coding to be executed at this point in the procedure sequence") state what a PROVIDED ENTER does at run time; no program reaches them, so nothing conforms to them, and the honest verdict is non-support of the element, witnessed by its named diagnostic. GR2 ("Implementors will specify, for their compilers, all details on how the other language(s) are to be written") is the closest to CONFORMS (a documentation duty discharged vacuously by specifying no language), but §1985:C.2 item (38) lists only SR1 ("Language-name-1 is specified by the implementor") as ENTER's implementor-defined element, so GR2 is a duty of an implementation that includes ENTER, which WiseOwl does not; it is DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT too." The siblings 1985-SR-VI.6.12.3-1 and -3 are re-recorded DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT in the same batch (kb/Work PB5373 class 3).

next.reason: 1985: "Implementors will specify, for their compilers, all details on how the other language(s) are to be written."; 2023: "No ENTER statement in 2023; no candidate covers other-language text written within COBOL source". 2023 has no ENTER statement clause. Candidates cover inter-language calls and pointers only, not other-language code written in a COBOL program, so the rule is gone.
